meta.task: 18 - dated before/after imagery and OSM context for the blamed drainage sites
meta.attribution: Esri World Imagery Wayback; imagery (c) Esri, Maxar, Earthstar Geographics and the GIS User Community

imagery.service: Esri World Imagery Wayback (public, no login)
imagery.release_vs_acquisition: release date != acquisition date; for every release the release's own metadata layer was queried (identify) at the site point to get the real acquisition date (SRC_DATE), source and resolution of the raster drawn at the chip zoom; releases deduped by acquisition date
imagery.chip: point: 500 x 500 m; line: bbox + 150 m; JPEG q85; marked copy = site geometry drawn as a thin outline. Point chips and station detail chips are native z18 (17 or lower when tiles are missing). Whole-corridor chips for lines are rendered at the highest zoom that fits 1200 px and downscaled to that cap, so long corridors are layout-level overviews; lines whose bbox + pad exceeds 1400 m additionally get native-z18 500 x 500 m detail chips at their start/mid/end stations, on the anchor dates only
imagery.dates_selected: every distinct acquisition date up to 10 per site: the closest date either side of the event date and of each image_windows bound, then an even spread
imagery.cloud_note: 'brightness' is a cloud/haze heuristic (fraction of near-white pixels), not an interpretation

osm.source: OpenStreetMap via Overpass, current data (not historical)
osm.setback_note: building count/area within 5/10/20 m of a mapped waterway is a setback proxy, NOT the legal setback
